# pbs_user (Resource)

Manages a Proxmox Backup Server user: an account of one of the server's realms — `pbs`, the server's own user database; `pam`, the accounts of the host; or an LDAP, Active Directory or OpenID Connect realm. Only users of the `pbs` realm have a password PBS stores; the others authenticate against their realm, and PBS keeps only the settings below.

A user has no privileges until ACL entries grant them, with `pbs_acl`. Its API tokens are `pbs_api_token` resources, and need ACL entries of their own.

~> **Destroying a user removes all its ACL entries.** PBS deletes a user's API tokens, and their ACL entries, along with the user, but keeps the user's own entries, which would apply again to a user created later under the same ID. Destroying this resource therefore first removes every ACL entry of the user, including entries Terraform does not manage; that needs Sys.Audit on /access/acl and Permissions.Modify on /access/acl, without which destroying fails. Replacing a user without changing `userid`, as `terraform apply -replace` does, also loses its tokens and the entries of `pbs_acl` resources: the next plan creates them again, the tokens with new secrets.

**Changing the password.** PBS takes `password_wo` when it creates the user, from any caller, API tokens included. Later it changes a password only through `PUT /access/password`, which is closed to API tokens: a change of `password_wo_version` needs a provider that signs in with `username` and `password`, and is a plan-time error with an API token. PBS wants the caller's own password as confirmation, which the provider sends, and the caller needs `Permissions.Modify on /access/users` — `root@pam` may change any password.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A user of PBS's own realm, for a Proxmox VE cluster. It has no privileges
# until pbs_acl grants them, and PVE signs in with an API token of it, which
# needs ACL entries of its own.
resource "pbs_user" "pve" {
  userid  = "pve@pbs"
  comment = "PVE cluster"
}

# A person who signs in to the web interface. The password is write-only: it
# never reaches the plan or state, and PBS receives it when the user is
# created and whenever password_wo_version changes. Changing it later needs a
# provider that signs in with a username and password, not an API token.
resource "pbs_user" "alice" {
  userid    = "alice@pbs"
  firstname = "Alice"
  lastname  = "Example"
  email     = "alice@example.com"

  password_wo         = var.alice_password
  password_wo_version = 1
}

# An account of the host, through the pam realm: it signs in with the host's
# password, and PBS keeps only its settings. It expires at the end of 2026.
resource "pbs_user" "operator" {
  userid = "operator@pam"
  expire = 1798761600
}

variable "alice_password" {
  description = "Initial password of alice@pbs, 8 to 64 characters."
  type        = string
  sensitive   = true
  ephemeral   = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `userid` (String) User ID: the user name, `@`, and the realm, such as `alice@pbs` or `backup@pam`. The realm must exist; a `pam` user also needs an account on the host to sign in. Changing it replaces the user.

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `comment` (String) Free-form comment, up to 128 characters on one line.
- `email` (String) Email address, 2 to 64 characters. PBS sends the user's notifications there.
- `enable` (Boolean) Whether the user may sign in. Defaults to `true`. The API tokens of a disabled user cannot sign in either.
- `expire` (Number) When the account expires, in seconds since the Unix epoch, such as the `unix` attribute of a `time_offset` resource; `0`, the default, means never. Like a disabled user, an expired one and its API tokens cannot sign in.
- `firstname` (String) First name, 2 to 64 characters.
- `lastname` (String) Last name, 2 to 64 characters.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Password of the user, 8 to 64 characters, for a user of the `pbs` realm only: users of other realms authenticate there. Write-only: Terraform passes it to PBS without storing it in the plan or state, and PBS never returns it, so a change made outside Terraform goes unnoticed. PBS receives it when the object is created and whenever `password_wo_version` changes. Requires `password_wo_version`, and Terraform or OpenTofu 1.11 or later.
- `password_wo_version` (Number) Version of `password_wo`, which Terraform stores in its place. Change it — increment it, say — to send a new `password_wo`; removing it, with `password_wo`, leaves the value on the server as it is. Requires `password_wo`.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same value as `userid`, present because Terraform requires an `id`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_user.pve
  identity = {
    userid = "pve@pbs"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `userid` (String) User ID, such as `alice@pbs`.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = pbs_user.pve
  id = "pve@pbs"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Users are imported by user ID, as the pbs_users data source or the Access
# Control panel shows it. PBS never returns a password, so password_wo_version
# is empty after an import, and a configuration that sets it plans a password
# change: with an API token that is a plan-time error, and with a password it
# replaces the user's current password. Leave password_wo and
# password_wo_version out of an imported user unless that is intended.
terraform import pbs_user.pve pve@pbs
```
